investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on 2-Node Subset
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval runner never reached the agent-creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod VMs. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new remote-agent pods. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not complete, leaving all four required evidence fields absent and triggering the contract validation error. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the 2 kata-capable nodes, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported by all three check messages reporting 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on exactly 2 nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to those 2 nodes before capacity is even considered. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, there is no fallback. Supported by the scheduler message '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all three checks.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: a prior eval run or user session may have left pods running that were not cleaned up, consuming the finite VM resource budget. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) implies cleanup is expected but may not have completed if a prior run was interrupted.

Lower confidence — node pool under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or real workloads schedule simultaneously against the same 2-node pool, transient exhaustion is possible even without leaks. No concurrent-load evidence is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on 2-Node Subset
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval runner never reached the agent-creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod VMs. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new remote-agent pods. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not complete, leaving all four required evidence fields absent and triggering the contract validation error. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the 2 kata-capable nodes, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported by all three check messages reporting 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on exactly 2 nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to those 2 nodes before capacity is even considered. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, there is no fallback. Supported by the scheduler message '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all three checks.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: a prior eval run or user session may have left pods running that were not cleaned up, consuming the finite VM resource budget. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) implies cleanup is expected but may not have completed if a prior run was interrupted.

Lower confidence — node pool under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or real workloads schedule simultaneously against the same 2-node pool, transient exhaustion is possible even without leaks. No concurrent-load evidence is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-26 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing from the check result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote agent pods (the other 4 nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector). With no available VM slots and no preemption victims found, every pod submitted by the eval scheduler was stuck Unschedulable for ~141–146 seconds before timing out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because no pod was ever scheduled, createAgent() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returned, and no evidence was collected against the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json lines 266–270.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no room for the eval's probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently constrained to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes have reduced capacity (e.g., after a node replacement, scale-down, or resource limit change), exhaustion becomes more likely.

Tertiary — concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all VM slots: if production traffic or other eval runs are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm leases at the time the eval fires, the eval pod will always be blocked until those leases are released.
Lower confidence — eval probe timing collision: if multiple eval runs overlap and each submits a remote agent pod simultaneously, they compete for the same limited VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes.
